questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Revolt of 1857:
1. The sepoys at Meerut began their march to Delhi on 19 April 1857.
2. Lord Canning was the Governor-General of India during the Revolt of 1857.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2 only.
  • Statement 1 is incorrect: The Meerut sepoys actually marched to Delhi on 10 May 1857, not 19 April.
  • Statement 2 is correct: Lord Canning was the Governor-General of India during the Revolt of 1857.

questions.question: The revolution of 1857 started in May from which of the following cantonments in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Meerut.
The 1857 Revolution, also known as the Indian Mutiny, began in Meerut on May 10, 1857, and spread to Delhi, Agra, Kanpur, and Lucknow. It was suppressed after the rebels were defeated in Gwalior on June 20, 1858.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Revolt of 1857:
1. Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi died fighting against the British at Kanpur.
2. Begum Hazrat Mahal played a prominent role in organizing the revolt in Awadh.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2 only.
  • Statement 1 is incorrect: Rani Lakshmibai did not die at Kanpur; she died fighting heroically at Gwalior in June 1858.
  • Statement 2 is correct: Begum Hazrat Mahal played a prominent role in organizing the revolt in Awadh.

questions.question: Which military officer led the British forces in the Battle of Chinhat fought in 1857?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Henry Lawrence.
The Battle of Chinhat took place on the morning of June 30, 1857, near the village of Chinhat in Awadh (now Uttar Pradesh), specifically at Ismaliganj, where British forces clashed with Indian rebels during the Indian Rebellion of 1857.

questions.question:
Match the following leaders with the regions they led during the Revolt of 1857:
LeadersRegion of Revolt
A. Rani Lakshmibai1. Bihar
B. Kunwar Singh2. Jhansi
C. Begum Hazrat Mahal3. Lucknow
D. Nana Saheb4. Kanpur
questions.solution:
The correct answer is A-2, B-1, C-3, D-4.
  • Rani Lakshmibai led the revolt in Jhansi (2).
  • Kunwar Singh led the revolt in Bihar (1).
  • Begum Hazrat Mahal led the revolt in Lucknow (3).
  • Nana Saheb led the revolt in Kanpur (4).

questions.question: Nana Sahib, a rebel at Kanpur was the son of which of the following Peshwas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Baji Rao II.
Bajirao II (10 January 1775 - 28 January 1851) was the last Peshwa of the Maratha Empire. Nana Sahib was his son.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Bahadur Shah II contributed to the Revolt of 1857.
Reason (R): He was the last Mughal emperor and was deposed and exiled by the British after the revolt.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.option_3: A is true, R is false
questions.option_4: A is false, R is true
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Bahadur Shah II, also known as Bahadur Shah Zafar, was the twentieth and final Mughal Emperor of India. During the Revolt of 1857, he played a symbolic role as a leader for the Indian rebels. Following the suppression of the uprising, the British deposed him and sent him into exile in Rangoon. His position as the last Mughal emperor is the reason he contributed to the revolt.

questions.question: The sepoys of Meerut arrived at the Gates of Red Fort to meet the Mughal emperor, Bahadur Shah on
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 11 May, 1857.
On 10 May 1857, the revolt broke out at Meerut. The very next day, i.e., on 11 May 1857, they marched to Delhi and reached the Red Fort. There they declared Bahadur Shah Zafar as the leader of the revolt.

questions.question: Whose proclamation of November 1, 1858 declared that thereafter India would be governed by and in the name of the British Monarch through a Secretary of State?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Queen Victoria's.
Issued on 1 November 1858 after the Revolt of 1857, this proclamation ended the East India Company's rule and transferred power to the British Crown. India would henceforth be governed in the name of Queen Victoria through the new office of Secretary of State for India, marking the start of Direct British Crown Rule (1858-1947).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Permanent Settlement introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793:
1. Under this system, zamindars were recognized as the owners of the land.
2. The Permanent Settlement was never extended to Punjab.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2.
  • Statement 1 is correct: Under the Permanent Settlement, zamindars were recognized as the owners of the land.
  • Statement 2 is correct: The system was implemented in Bengal, Bihar, and parts of Odisha, but never extended to Punjab.

questions.question: Who among the following devised the system of 'Subsidiary Alliance'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lord Wellesley.
He devised the Subsidiary Alliance as a system in 1798. Under this system, Indian rulers were required to maintain British forces within their territory and adhere to British political advice. States that accepted the alliance included Hyderabad (1798), Mysore (1799), Awadh (1801), Peshwa (1802), Bhosle and Scindia (1803).

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Raja Ram Mohan Roy played a major role in the abolition of the practice of Sati.
Reason (R): Lord William Bentinck, as Governor-General, passed the Bengal Sati Regulation Act in 1829, which legally banned Sati in British India.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.option_3: A is true, but R is false
questions.option_4: A is false, but R is true
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Lord William Bentinck was appointed Governor-General in 1828. On December 4, 1829, he enacted the Bengal Sati Regulation, which formally abolished the practice of Sati across British India. Raja Ram Mohan Roy's persistent efforts and campaigns against Sati greatly influenced this decision.

questions.question: The Doctrine of Lapse was an annexation policy devised by which of the following Governor-Generals of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lord Dalhousie.
The Doctrine of Lapse was an annexation policy used by the British East India Company to expand its empire in India. Under this policy, if a ruler of a dependent state died without a male heir, the state would be annexed by the British. States annexed under the policy: Satara (1848), Jaitpur and Sambalpur (1849), Baghat (1850), Udaipur (1852), Jhansi (1854), Nagpur (1854), Tanjore, and Arcot (1855).

questions.question:
Match the following personalities with their contributions in British India:
List IList II (Contribution)
A. Robert Clive1. First Surveyor General of Bengal, prepared Bengal Atlas (1779)
B. Warren Hastings2. Served twice as Governor of Bengal and led the Battle of Plassey (1757)
C. James Rennel3. Governor-General credited with administrative and judicial reforms
D. Lord Dalhousie4. Governor-General associated with major reforms and expansion policies
questions.solution:
The correct answer is A-2, B-3, C-1, D-4.
  • Robert Clive served twice as Governor of Bengal (1758-60 and 1764-67) and led the Battle of Plassey for the British East India Company in 1757.
  • Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal credited with administrative and judicial reforms.
  • James Rennel, the first Surveyor General of Bengal (1767-1777), is renowned for his Bengal Atlas (1779).
  • Lord Dalhousie was associated with major reforms and expansion policies like the Doctrine of Lapse and laying the foundation of railways.

questions.question: The Daroga system in 1792 was introduced by whom among the following Governor-Generals in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lord Cornwallis (1786-93).
The system of Daroga was introduced as part of Police reforms. Police of each district were placed under District Judge. Each district was divided into Thanas/Police circles which were headed by Daroga. He also abolished District Faujdari Courts and set up circuit courts in Calcutta, Dacca, Murshidabad, and Patna.

questions.question: Who is called the father of Local Self-Government in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lord Ripon.
During Lord Ripon's tenure (1880-84), key reforms included the repeal of the Vernacular Press Act (1881) and a resolution on local self-government (1882), which earned him the title 'father of Local Self-Government in India'. His period also saw the Ilbert Bill controversy (1883).

questions.question: Which of the following Governor-Generals of British India was in favour of free press and repealed the press regulations of 1823?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lord Metcalfe (1835-36).
Lord Metcalfe is also known as the 'Liberator of Indian Press'. The Licensing Regulation ordinance of 1823 was brought out by acting Governor-General John Adams. Lord Metcalfe repealed these regulations, favoring a free press.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Lord Dalhousie is regarded as the father of Indian Railways.
2. The first railway line in India was opened in 1853 between Bombay and Thane, covering 21 miles (34 km).
3. The first railway line in South India was opened in 1856.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 3.
  • Lord Dalhousie (1848-1856) is regarded as the 'father of Indian Railways' and was instrumental in developing the railway network.
  • The first railway line in India ran 21 miles (34 km) from Bombay to Thane in 1853.
  • The first railway line in South India was inaugurated in 1856.

questions.question: In the context of British rule in India, who among the following Governor-Generals created a professional cadre of company servants making provisions for them for generous salaries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lord Cornwallis (1786 - 1793).
He is also regarded as the 'Father of Civil Service in India' for his role in shaping the civil service system by creating a professional cadre of company servants with generous salaries to reduce corruption.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Victoria Memorial Hall in Kolkata:
1. Lord Curzon entrusted William Emerson as its architect.
2. The foundation stone was laid by the Prince of Wales in 1906.
3. It was completed and opened to the public in 1921.
4. It was built to commemorate Queen Victoria's reign in India.
Which of the above statements are true?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1, 2, 3 and 4.
The Victoria Memorial, constructed between 1906 and 1921 in Kolkata, West Bengal, was envisioned by Viceroy George Curzon to honor Queen Victoria's 25-year reign in India. Its foundation stone was laid in 1906 by the Prince of Wales (later King George V), and it was inaugurated for the public in 1921.

questions.question: Who among the following was the Viceroy of British India when the Shimla conference was held in 1945?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lord Wavell (1944 to 1947).
The Shimla Conference was held from June 25 to July 14, 1945, at Viceregal Lodge in Shimla, India, during Lord Wavell's tenure as Viceroy.

questions.question:
Match List-1 with List-11.
List-I (Governor General)List-II (Period)
A. Warren Hastings1. 1772-1785
B. Lord Cornwallis2. 1786-1793
C. Sir John Shore3. 1793-1798
D. Lord Wellesley4. 1798-1805
questions.solution:
The correct answer is A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4.
  • The first Governor of Bengal was Robert Clive.
  • The first Governor General of Bengal in 1773 was Warren Hastings (1772-1785).
  • The first Governor General of India was William Bentinck.
  • The first Viceroy of India was Lord Canning.

questions.question:
Identify the INCORRECTLY matched pair(s) of the British Governor-Generals of India and the events with which they are associated.
i) Lord Dalhousie - Revolt of 1857
ii) Lord Auckland - First Afghan War
iii) Lord Canning - Wood's Despatch 1854
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Only (i) and (iii).
  • Lord Dalhousie (1848-1856) is associated with the Doctrine of Lapse and Wood's Despatch 1854, not the Revolt of 1857 (which happened in 1857 under Lord Canning).
  • Lord Canning was the Governor-General during the Revolt of 1857; Wood's Despatch was in 1854 under Lord Dalhousie.
  • Lord Auckland is correctly associated with the First Afghan War (1836-1842).

questions.question: English as the official language of India for higher education was incorporated in the resolution formulation by
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lord Macaulay.
Lord Macaulay is considered to be the founder of the British education system in India. His Macaulay's Minute of 1835 recommended English as the medium of instruction for higher education. He was also the chairman of the first Law Commission of pre-independent India.

questions.question: The Vernacular Press Act was enacted during the regime of which viceroy of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lord Lytton (1876-1880).
The Vernacular Press Act (also known as the 'Gagging Act') was enacted in 1878. The act allowed the government to confiscate the assets of newspapers in case of publishing anything 'objectionable'.
